reading: Stated rental income and estate income are not qualified business income: whether a rental is a section 162 trade or business (26 U.S.C. 199A(d)(1)) is not stated. Tax-Calculator gets rent in e02000 only (not e26270 or e27200); TAXSIM gets rent and estate income in `intrec`, either sign. PolicyEngine's default counts rent as qualified business income (rental_income_would_be_qualified defaults to true) and estate income not.

reading: A filer with a 401(k) deferral (traditional or Roth) is an active participant in an employer plan for the IRA deduction limit (26 U.S.C. 219(g)(5)); a filer with none is not, since no other plan coverage is stated.

Rul. 2025-4); with them the 2.15.17 value is $40,217.95.
